The initiative aims to mobilise $100 million and provide three years of support through unrestricted grants, allowing recipients to direct resources towards their priorities. Its approach focuses on strengthening organisations and healthcare systems while addressing barriers that prevent women and girls from accessing essential services and living free from violence.The Women's Health Co-Lab was launched on September 29, 2025, by ICONIQ Impact, the philanthropic platform associated with investment firm ICONIQ, in partnership with Co-Impact, a global collaborative philanthropy organisation.The initiative brings together philanthropists to support organisations addressing persistent inequalities in women's health and safety.French Gates and her daughters were among the founding supporters, alongside other philanthropists and families. The initiative's initial commitments exceeded $70 million, with a broader target of raising $100 million. The funding was designed to support 22 selected organisations over three years, giving them resources to expand their programmes and strengthen the systems serving women and girls.The Women's Health Co-Lab focuses on maternal health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and gender-based violence. Its grants support organisations providing services, advocating policy changes and addressing barriers that affect women's wellbeing.Six organisations were selected to improve maternal healthcare, strengthen service delivery and help women access appropriate care during pregnancy and childbirth.One recipient is Every Mother Counts, a nonprofit working to make pregnancy and childbirth safer. Its work addresses barriers that prevent women from receiving quality maternal healthcare, including gaps in access, resources and support.Ten organisations will work to expand access to reproductive healthcare, contraception, reliable information and related services. Their work also includes advocacy to address policies and social barriers that restrict women's ability to make decisions about their health.Among the named recipients are Americans for Contraception and Girl Effect, which works with adolescent girls through media and community programmes.Six organisations were selected to strengthen efforts to prevent violence against women and girls, support survivors and challenge harmful social norms. Their work includes community programmes, advocacy and efforts to improve protections for those at risk.Named recipients include Ujamaa Africa, which works to prevent gender-based violence through programmes in African communities, and Serenas, an organisation working in this field.A central feature of the Women's Health Co-Lab is its use of unrestricted funding. Instead of requiring recipients to spend every dollar on a narrowly defined activity, the initiative allows organisations greater flexibility to decide how the money can best support their work.This approach is intended to reduce administrative burdens and help organisations respond to changing circumstances. A group working on maternal health may need to strengthen healthcare delivery, while an organisation focused on violence prevention may prioritise community education, survivor support or policy advocacy.Co-Impact worked with recipients to refine their plans and budgets as part of the grantmaking process. The collaborative approach gives organisations a role in determining how the funding can best advance their objectives.Ujamaa Africa was among the organisations selected for funding, receiving an unrestricted grant of $3 million. The organisation works to prevent gender-based violence through programmes that engage young people and communities.Its executive director, Benjamin Omondi Mboya, said the funding would help the organisation expand its programmes across Kenya, Malawi and Somaliland.The grant illustrates how flexible funding can help organisations adapt their programmes to local needs rather than relying entirely on short-term, tightly restricted project grants.The founding donor group included Tricia Black and Patrick Brogan, Marie Dageville, Rachel Markham and Cedric Dageville, Holly Fogle and Jeff Lieberman, Barrie Glabman and Adam Schwartz, Susan Long Hall and C. David Hall, Renee and Alexis Lê-Quôc, Aarti Lohia, Diksha and Divesh Makan, Samantha McManus and David Karp, Andrea Meditch, Rick and Nancy Moskovitz, Susan and Erin Samueli, and the Tullman family.ICONIQ Impact helped bring the donors together, while Co-Impact contributed experience in supporting organisations working to strengthen health, education and economic systems. Their partnership reflects an approach in which multiple donors pool resources around shared priorities.Women's health outcomes are influenced by more than access to medical treatment. Maternal care, reproductive health services and protection from violence are also shaped by healthcare infrastructure, public policy, social attitudes and economic circumstances.Organisations working in these areas often require sustained support to train healthcare workers, provide services, advocate for policy changes and reach underserved communities. The Co-Lab's three-year funding model is intended to give recipients greater scope to plan and expand their work.
Article Summary: The Women's Health Co-Lab focuses on maternal health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and gender-based violence. Melinda French Gates and her daughters were among the founding supporters, alongside other philanthropists and families. The initiative aims to mobilise $100 million and provide three years of support through unrestricted grants, allowing recipients to direct resources towards their priorities.

Article Title: A battered 1677 wooden cabinet looked like an ordinary old box; one photograph of its original key helped Sotheby’s identify a rare piece that sold for $1.64 million
Article Text:
PC: Sotheby's

What made the battered 1677 wooden cabinet worth $1.64 million

How did the cabinet’s original key prove it was a rare 17th-century piece

PC: Sotheby's

Why did Sotheby’s sell the 1677 wooden cabinet for $1.64 million in 2026

A small carved oak cabinet made in Salem, Massachusetts, in 1677 reached Sotheby’s as a few photographs submitted through its online portal. To an untrained eye, it might have looked like a grungy old box. Then Erik Gronning, a senior advisor in Sotheby’s American Furniture, Folk Art and Decorative Arts Department, saw the last image: the cabinet’s original key. It was, he says, the moment he knew for certain it was a period piece. In January 2026, the Symon and Rebeckah Horne Pilgrim Century Valuables Cabinet sold for $1,636,000, the highest price for American furniture in more than a decade.According to Sotheby's, the piece is titled the Highly Important Symon and Rebeckah Horne Pilgrim Century Valuables Cabinet. It is attributed to the Symonds shops in Salem and dated 1677. Sotheby's records the sale price as $1,636,000. An untrained eye might read the object as a grungy old box. Sotheby's states that it is one of only five known examples attributed to the Symonds shops, and the only one to survive with its original key.The carved door bears the initials of Symon and Rebeckah Horne, an Andover couple, on either side of a small heart.Erik Gronning, a senior advisor in Sotheby's American Furniture, Folk Art and Decorative Arts Department, says the heart was included to symbolise the couple's love. Above it is the date the Hornes had the cabinet made: 1677, the year their son was born.The submitted photographs included an image of the cabinet's original key. Gronning recalls his first reaction to the submission, saying, "I did not believe it was real when I saw it." He says it was the final submitted image, the one showing the original key, that made him certain the cabinet was a period piece and a highly important one.The cabinet to the Symonds shops and says it is the only one of the five known examples to retain its original key. In the account Sotheby's gives, a single photograph therefore moved the cabinet from an object that appeared ordinary to one that its specialist regarded as of high importance.The cabinet descended through the Horne family for generations. It later passed to a local historical society, which the article says had quietly held it for some sixty years before deciding to let it go. The piece then came to Sotheby's through the submissions portal.The sale took place in 2026, and the final price was $1,636,000. The auction house describes this as the highest price for American furniture in more than ten years. Sotheby's presents the cabinet alongside four other portal submissions: a Ten Commandments tablet, a Claude Lalanne armchair, a Rolex Daytona and a Qianlong-period Chinese vase.
Article Summary: The Symon and Rebeckah Horne Pilgrim Century Valuables Cabinet sold for $1,636,000 in 2026. Sotheby's says it is one of only five known examples attributed to the Symonds shops in Salem, Massachusetts, and the only one to survive with its original key. It is the highest price for American furniture in more than ten years.

Article Title: Jennifer Garner bought back her family’s 55-acre Oklahoma farm in 2017; the land, held by her family since 1936, now inspires her organic children’s food business
Article Text:
PC: Forbes

Garner’s family farm has been in Oklahoma since 1936

How Garner joined the company behind organic children’s food

The family farm behind Garner’s farm-to-food philosophy

Once Upon a Farm expands its reach while focusing on nutrition access

Jennifer Garner’s work with organic children’s food has a connection to a place that has been part of her family’s life for generations.In Locust Grove, Oklahoma, a family farm that has been in Garner’s family since 1936 has helped shape her understanding of where food comes from and how children might develop a closer relationship with farming. Garner, who joined Once Upon a Farm as a co-founder in 2017, has spoken about the importance of making nutritious food more accessible to families. The business began with a practical problem: its original founders struggled to find the kind of organic baby food they wanted in local shops. Years later, the company has expanded across the United States, while Garner’s family farm remains a source of inspiration for its products.The Oklahoma property has been in Garner’s family located in Locust Grove; it has remained more than a backdrop to the actress’s childhood memories. Her uncle Robert still lives there and manages the farm, preserving a connection between the land and the family’s everyday life.Garner has described, "Once I started working for Once Upon a Farm, I loved the idea of connecting kids to the farm early on. And so here we are, connecting kids to the farm and it gets to be my family’s farm that’s been with us since 1936.One thing that I love about the farm is that my Uncle Robert still lives here. He is the holder of the stories and runs the farm to this day."Once Upon a Farm has developed into a national brand, the family’s agricultural roots offer a more personal reference point for its emphasis on organic ingredients and childhood nutrition.Once Upon a Farm was founded in 2015 by Cassandra Curtis and Ari Raz. Curtis wanted better options for her daughter after finding that the baby food available in nearby supermarkets did not meet her expectations. She began developing recipes herself, eventually bringing cold-pressure-protected baby food to retail shelves.Garner became involved in 2017, alongside John Foraker, the former chief executive of organic food company Annie’s. Foraker brought experience in building and scaling a consumer food business, while Garner offered the perspective of a parent who had encountered similar questions about what to feed young children.The company’s range has since grown beyond its original baby food products. It now includes organic snacks, smoothies and meals for children at different stages, with products distributed through major retailers across the country. Once Upon a Farm has described its aim as making nutritious food easier for families to find and serve.For Garner, the connection between agriculture and childhood nutrition has been a recurring theme in her work with the company. Her family’s Oklahoma farm provides a tangible example of where food begins, rather than presenting it solely as a finished product on a supermarket shelf.In material published by Once Upon a Farm, Garner spoke about wanting children to develop an early connection with farming. The fact that her own family’s property has remained in use for decades gives that idea a personal dimension. Her uncle’s continued involvement also means that farming knowledge has not been separated from the place where it was acquired.Once Upon a Farm has built its range around organic produce and refrigerated products, distinguishing its approach from the shelf-stable baby food that has long occupied a large part of the market.Once Upon a Farm’s expansion has taken it well beyond its original retail footprint. By August 2026, Forbes reported that the company was selling more than 40 products in over 25,000 stores. Its portfolio had grown to include drinkable smoothies and oat bars, alongside food for babies and young children.As reported by Forbes, the company also entered the public markets in February 2026, with an initial public offering valued at approximately $724 million. Garner marked the occasion at the New York Stock Exchange, but told Forbes that she preferred to concentrate on the company’s operations rather than follow daily movements in its share price.She holds a reported 7% stake in the business and serves as chief brand officer. Her responsibilities have included working with retailers and helping communicate the company’s purpose to families. Forbes estimated her stake to be worth about $55 million in its August 2026 report, although the value of publicly traded shares can change.Access to nutritious food has also become part of the company’s work. Garner told Forbes that obtaining certification for the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children, commonly known as WIC, was a major priority. The programme helps eligible low-income families buy approved foods, and Once Upon a Farm had secured certification in more than 20 states by the time of the report.
Article Summary: Jennifer Garner joined Once Upon a Farm as a co-founder in 2017. The company was founded in 2015 by Cassandra Curtis and Ari Raz. It sells organic snacks, smoothies and meals for children at different stages. Garner’s family farm in Oklahoma has been in her family since 1936.

Article Title: WordPress cofounder Matt Mullenweg is buying Stewart Brand’s 1912 Sausalito houseboat; Mirene was once a gasoline schooner and later became a restored home on the water
Article Text:
Representative Image of the historic houseboat Mirene docked along Sausalito’s scenic waterfront ( AI Generrated Image)

A century-old tugboat with an unusual history

From $1.8 million to a $1 million asking price

A houseboat purchase amid upheaval at Automattic

Matt Mullenweg, the cofounder of WordPress and chief executive of Automattic, is set to acquire Mirene, a historic houseboat that has been home to Whole Earth Catalog creator Stewart Brand and his partner, Ryan Phelan, for decades. Built in Coos Bay, Oregon, and completed in 1912, Mirene was originally a gasoline schooner intended to serve canneries in Alaska. It was converted into a diesel tugboat in the 1930s. Mullenweg confirmed in a September 11 blog post that he had made an offer for the vessel, and The San Francisco Standard reported on September 16 that the deal was under contract. The purchase also involves the couple’s smaller houseboat, although the agreed price for the vessels has not been disclosed. For Brand and Phelan, the planned sale marks the end of a long chapter shaped by restoration, life on the water and their connection to Sausalito’s distinctive houseboat community.Mirene is no ordinary houseboat. Brand and Phelan acquired the vessel in the early 1980s and spent decades restoring it, adapting it into a home while retaining its ability to sail. Its history and seaworthiness distinguish it from the stationary houseboats around it.According to The San Francisco Standard, Mirene is the only houseboat in Sausalito permitted to leave its dock. The couple spent years restoring and adapting the vessel for life on the water. Its working-boat origins remain part of its character, setting it apart from the stationary houseboats around it.The vessel also carries a piece of music lore. According to The San Francisco Standard, a wooden table added by the couple is supposedly where Otis Redding sat while writing “(Sittin’ on) the Dock of the Bay” during a stay on a nearby houseboat. The anecdote adds to Mirene’s appeal, although the precise connection between the table and the song remains a reported story rather than an independently established fact. The smaller houseboat included in the planned transaction offers a different arrangement. Unlike Mirene, the smaller houseboat is stationary. The San Francisco Standard described it as having a well-lit living area. Mullenweg has said he hopes to blog from Mirene’s kitchen table, making the vessel both a place to live and a setting for his writing. In an earlier interview with The San Francisco Standard in November 2025, Phelan discussed the sense of loss associated with parting with the vessel.The planned sale followed an extended period on the market. Mirene was initially listed for $1.8 million before its asking price was reduced by $100,000 in July. In August, the price fell again to $1 million. The smaller houseboat’s asking price also fell from $700,000 to $450,000, according to its listing. The reductions did not establish the final sale price. When The San Francisco Standard reported the deal on September 16, the transaction was under contract, and the parties had not disclosed the amount agreed upon.Compass real estate agent Steve Sekhon told the publication that the boats had attracted no offers for almost a year, despite their refurbished condition. He said the price reduction helped bring the listings greater visibility. The report also described improving activity in the local houseboat market, with sales generally closing slightly below asking prices. The smaller vessel was described by real estate agent Steve Sekhon as a potential privacy buffer for the buyer of Mirene or a separate waterfront retreat for someone seeking a home in the Sausalito area. For a buyer interested in the area’s houseboat lifestyle, the two properties offer different ways to experience it: one aboard a vessel with a history of sailing, the other in a stationary home on the water.The purchase comes as Mullenweg navigates a period of corporate turmoil. In September, Automattic’s board voted to place him on paid leave as CEO, temporarily naming chief financial officer Mark Davies as interim chief executive. Mullenweg returned to the role roughly 33 hours later, after the attempted leadership change unravelled. The attempted leadership change was followed by the departure of directors involved in the dispute, with those departures reported around September 14. Automattic announced a new board on September 25, according to TechCrunch. Automattic is the parent company of WordPress.com, Tumblr and WooCommerce, among other businesses.Despite the disruption, Mullenweg has publicly embraced the prospect of taking on Mirene. In his September 11 blog post, Mullenweg wrote about the prospect of owning the vessel and the lessons he expected to learn from maintaining it. He also wrote that he hoped to do a lot of blogging from the kitchen table. Brand and Phelan now live primarily on a waterfront property in Petaluma, while Phelan has also bought another Sausalito houseboat, allowing her to maintain a connection with the community. Mullenweg has expressed the hope that he can eventually pass Mirene on to another steward decades from now.For now, the proposed sale brings together two people with an interest in independent publishing and the unconventional spaces in which creative work happens. If completed, the transaction will give Mullenweg a historic vessel shaped by more than a century of use, as well as a new place to write and live on the water. Brand, meanwhile, has said he expects the boat to bring its new owner good luck.
Article Summary: Matt Mullenweg, the cofounder of WordPress and chief executive of Automattic, is set to acquire Mirene, a historic houseboat that has been home to Whole Earth Catalog creator Stewart Brand and his partner, Ryan Phelan. The purchase also involves the couple's smaller houseboat, although the agreed price for the vessels has not been disclosed. The couple spent years restoring and adapting the vessel for life on the water.

Article Title: The Asian silktree was brought to America for its delicate pink flowers; its seeds can remain viable for up to nearly 150 years under dry storage
Article Text:
Image(s): Wikipedia

How this pink-flowering Asian silktree arrived in North America

Why the 1745 introduction date is often repeated while another source places the arrival around 1785

Rosea Mimosa blossoms along the ramp from southbound Interstate 95 (New Jersey Turnpike Eastern Spur) to westbound Interstate 280 (Essex Freeway) in the New Jersey Meadowlands, within Kearny, Hudson County, New Jersey (Image: Wikipedia)

How silktree took hold across the United States, from the Southeast to New York, Utah, and California

Why silktree thrives on disturbed roadsides, old fields, and forest edges via seeds and root sprouts

Why silktree populations rise and fall: short lifespans, a root-infecting fungus, and shade tolerance

Few garden trees look as graceful as the silktree in midsummer, when its fern-like leaves carry soft pink pompom flowers that seem to float above the branches. That beauty explains why people carried the tree across the ocean from Asia centuries ago and planted it beside homes and in gardens. Yet the same traits that made it appealing, including fast growth, abundant seeds, and tolerance of poor conditions, also allowed it to wander beyond yards. Today it appears along roadsides, in old fields, and at forest edges.The US Department of Agriculture states this tree does not belong to North America. It is native to Asia and occurs from Iran to Japan, and its scientific name is Albizia julibrissin. The review lists mimosa and silky acacia as other common names, and it notes that the genus is sometimes spelt with a double z, likely because the genus honors a man who introduced silktree to Tuscany, Italy. Silktree is a deciduous, nitrogen-fixing tree or shrub, usually between three and fifteen metres tall, with a broad crown. Its showy flowerheads form clusters at the ends of branches, and each head holds fifteen to twenty-five flowers.The US Department of Agriculture treats the arrival date with care. It states that silktree was introduced as an ornamental in the eighteenth century, and it acknowledges that many sources assert a specific year, 1745, for its introduction to the United States.It then adds a different account from Cothran, who wrote that the tree was brought to North America about 1785 and was first offered for sale in 1807. Either account places the introduction in the 1700s. By the 1950s, silktree was established locally in Georgia; it was a new record in Oconee County, South Carolina, in 1972, and it was first reported in the flora of Connecticut in 2008. In between, it was described as newly documented around Washington, District of Columbia, in 1995.By 2010, the US Department of Agriculture also reports silktree occurred as far north as New York and Massachusetts, in southern parts of the Midwest, throughout the south-central and southeastern United States excluding tropical Florida, and in New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, and California. The distribution and effects of silktree are best documented in the Southeast, where inventory data collected from 2001 to 2008 showed it is most common in north-central Alabama. Cold limits the tree to low elevations. In the Southeast, it does not typically grow above about 900 to 1,000 metres, and in Great Smoky Mountains National Park it was common between 370 and 610 metres and absent above 740 metres. Cold also matters in Connecticut, where it typically kills seedlings in their first winter, although silktree has established near the milder coast.Silktree reproduces from seeds and regenerates by sprouting from roots after the top of the tree is killed or injured. Several authors note that it produces many seeds, and one source reports 8,000 seeds a year. Seeds fall mainly by gravity and secondarily travel by wind, water, and animals, with observations in Georgia suggesting wind can carry them at least ninety metres. A hard seed coat keeps seeds dormant until damaged by heat, fungi, soaking, or acid, and a small percentage of seeds kept in dry storage stayed viable for seventy to nearly one hundred fifty years. The circumstantial evidence suggests disturbance aids seedling establishment, and it describes silktree as an early to mid-successional species found on old fields, old homesites, roadsides, and woodland edges.Silktree is not an unstoppable force, and the US Department of Agriculture explains why. It is apparently short-lived in the United States because a soil-borne fungus called Fusarium infects the root system, causing wilting and eventually death. Researchers around Athens, Georgia, suggest silktree often dies back within ten to twenty years, while another report gives an average lifespan of about thirty years. Even so, trees killed by the wilt disease may leave behind a mass of root sprouts. Silktree also tolerates only partial shade and rarely occurs under a full canopy, which is why it favours open and disturbed ground. It may establish or increase on recently burned, thinned, or logged forest sites, and it was considered a potentially high threat to oak-hickory woodlands.
Article Summary: Silktree is a deciduous, nitrogen-fixing tree or shrub, usually between three and fifteen metres tall, with a broad crown. Its showy flowerheads form clusters at the ends of branches, and each head holds fifteen to twenty-five flowers. It is native to Asia and occurs from Iran to Japan.

Article Title: US court orders Trump administration to cancel taxpayer-funded political ads
Article Text: A US court on Sunday ordered the Donald Trump administration to cancel television commercials funded with millions of dollars in taxpayer money to promote the president's political message.US district judge Jennifer L Rochon in New York issued a temporary restraining order directing the administration to cancel any remaining ads, including those scheduled to air on Sunday night."Defendants shall not enter into, renew, or expand any agreement authorizing the development, creation, dissemination, placement, or airing of the challenged advertisements" during the two-week period covered by the order, the judge said.The order came after nonpartisan watchdog Common Cause challenged the ads, calling them an illegal misuse of taxpayer funds.In a court filing late Saturday, the justice department argued that a temporary restraining order was unnecessary because "the alleged offending conduct will end tomorrow".The department of homeland security allocated $20 million in taxpayer money for the advertisements.The money used for the ads came from a $175 million package Congress allocated to the department as part of Trump's immigration enforcement agenda.The White House has defended the commercials as public service announcements, similar to those used by previous administrations to promote government policies.However, the recent ads differ from many past public service announcements because they are not aimed at helping the public access or benefit from specific government programmes. One of the commercials closely replicates an advertisement Trump ran during his 2024 presidential re-election campaign.
Article Summary: US district judge Jennifer L Rochon in New York issued a temporary restraining order directing the administration to cancel any remaining ads. The department of homeland security allocated $20 million in taxpayer money for the advertisements. One of the commercials closely replicates an advertisement Trump ran during his 2024 presidential re-election campaign.

Article Title: Why did Pakistan declare Emergency in Imran Khan's bastion Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Article Text:
Emergency in Imran Khan’s bastion: Why Shehbaz Sharif’s govt took control of KP

PTI leaders arrested after emergency announcement

Imran Khan’s stronghold at the centre of political battle

Pakistan's political battle with jailed former prime minister Imran Khan has taken a sharp turn, with the Shehbaz Sharif government suspending his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led administration in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and imposing governor's rule in the province.The move brings one of Imran Khan's strongest political strongholds under direct control of the Shehbaz Sharif-led government, further deepening the confrontation between the military-backed government and PTI.Amid growing insecurities within the Shehbaz Sharif-Asim Munir duo, Imran Khan’s party has lost control of a province with around 40 million people, turning the region into the latest flashpoint in Pakistan’s political unrest.Thousands of people have taken to the streets in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa since early October, demanding Imran Khan’s release and protesting the military’s counter-insurgency operations along the border with Afghanistan.The Pakistan government has defended the move, citing the worsening law and order situation and accusing the provincial administration of failing to act against terrorism. Militants linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), an ideological ally of the Afghan Taliban, have killed thousands of security personnel and civilians in recent years.“The Cabinet took a detailed review of the deteriorating law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the circumstances arising from the provincial government’s deliberate indifference in the war against terrorism,” the office of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said in a statement.However, figures compiled by the Islamabad-based Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS) paint a different picture of the security situation in the province, as Financial Times reported.Civilian and security personnel deaths in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa stood at 485 in the first nine months of 2026, down 16% from the same period in 2025. Across Pakistan, such deaths rose by 9%, according to the think-tank.Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari approved the emergency on the prime minister’s advice. His office cited a “failure of negotiations” between the Pakistan government and PTI leaders in the province.Under governor’s rule, the governor, who is appointed by the Pakistan government, takes over the province’s administration. Pakistan’s interior ministry said the army would deploy personnel to help run the province and protect public property and government installations.Talal Chaudhry, junior interior minister, told the Financial Times that the move was a “routine measure” intended to help provincial authorities carry out their responsibilities, particularly in the fight against terrorism.The political confrontation intensified soon after the announcement, with reports emerging that senior PTI leaders had been arrested.An account on X associated with Junaid Akbar, a member of parliament and president of PTI’s provincial chapter, said he and provincial chief minister Sohail Afridi had been taken into custody.Afridi, 37, had been leading a long march across the province in support of Khan and against military operations that PTI claims have caused civilian deaths and damage. He is the youngest-ever chief minister of Pakistan and comes from the tribal belt bordering Afghanistan.Just hours before his government was suspended, Afridi had vowed to continue the march until the protesters’ demands were met.“There is no option other than accepting our demands,” Afridi said in a post on X.“We will not back down,” he said. “Our long march will continue until the demands are met, in accordance with the law. Here, only Imran Khan’s policy will prevail.”Pakistan’s interior ministry and armed forces did not respond to requests for comment, the Financial Times reported.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been a key political base for Imran Khan's PTI, which has governed the province since 2013. The party won more than 60% of the seats in the provincial assembly in the 2024 elections, two years after Khan was removed as prime minister through a parliamentary no-confidence vote.The former World Cup-winning cricket captain continues to be widely regarded as Pakistan’s most popular politician. Candidates backed by him won the largest number of seats in the national assembly in 2024.However, they were kept out of power as the military and the country’s two dominant dynastic political parties shaped the post-election arrangement, according to the Financial Times.The FT also cited analysts as saying PTI would comfortably win a competitive general election.PTI has accused the Shehbaz Sharif government of using security concerns as a pretext to remove its elected administration in the province.“The arrest of chief minister Sohail Afridi and Junaid Akbar has exposed the political nature of the government’s actions,” PTI spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram said in a statement.“These measures are not directed at addressing security challenges; they are intended to weaken PTI, undermine the elected government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and disregard the democratic will of its people.”
Article Summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is one of Imran Khan's strongest political strongholds. Shehbaz Sharif-led government has imposed governor's rule in the province. Reports emerge that senior PTI leaders have been arrested. Pakistan government has defended the move, citing the worsening law and order situation.

Article Title: Pak crisis: Shehbaz govt declares emergency, ends Imran Khan's party's rule in KPK
Article Text:
PTI has been mobilising supporters to pressure the federal government over Khan's imprisonment

Terrorism, law and order cited

PTI protests, warns of bloodshed

Pakistan on Sunday declared an emergency in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), suspending the provincial government led by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party amid deteriorating law and order and a growing confrontation with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government.President Asif Ali Zardari issued the proclamation under Articles 232(1) and 234(1) of the Constitution, citing rising terrorist attacks and a breakdown of constitutional machinery in the province. The move strips the elected provincial administration of its powers, with the chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general required to vacate their offices.Following the announcement the Pak government order the deployment of army in the province.The decision comes as thousands of PTI supporters march towards Islamabad, demanding Khan's release and access to medical treatment for the former prime minister, who has been in prison since 2023 on corruption and other charges. The party has described the cases against him as politically motivated. The emergency also follows failed negotiations between PTI and the federal government over the planned protest.The presidential declaration said the emergency had been imposed because of the grave security situation and the provincial government's alleged failure to tackle militancy.“The extraordinary intensity of terrorist incidents poses serious threats to the lives and property of the public,” the declaration stated.PTI has been mobilising supporters to pressure the federal government over Khan's imprisonment. KPK chief minister Sohail Afridi is leading the protest march, which began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 and has passed through several districts.The party had initially planned to take the march to Islamabad for a sit-in, but authorities have erected roadblocks using shipping containers at entry points to the capital and other locations. Two rounds of talks between PTI and the government failed to break the deadlock.Zulfikar Bukhari, a close Khan aide and PTI spokesman, called the emergency a “ridiculous decision”, saying KPK had the country's “only legitimately elected government”.“This will only lead to further bloodshed, instability and collateral damage,” he said, adding that there had always been room for talks but the decision showed negotiations were never the government's intention.Previous protests by Khan's supporters have turned violent, with security personnel and civilians killed during demonstrations in 2024.
Article Summary: President Asif Ali Zardari declares emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Suspends provincial government led by Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party. Decision comes as thousands of PTI supporters march towards Islamabad, demanding Khan's release.

Article Title: ‘No contact, no update’: Imran Khan’s son says father silent for 6 months, aunts remain ‘abducted’
Article Text:
Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest

Kasim says protests will continue

Sisters detained ahead of PTI protest

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan’s son Kasim Khan has claimed that his three aunts remain “abducted” by Pakistani authorities, saying their family and lawyers have received no information about their condition or the reasons for their detention. He also said he and his brother have had no contact with their father for more than six months.Kasim Khan made the remarks on Thursday, weeks after his aunts Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned September 27 protest and march to Islamabad.The demonstrations were called to demand updates on Imran Khan's health and his release from Adiala Jail, where the former prime minister has been incarcerated since August 2023.In a post on X, Kasim Khan linked the continued detention of his aunts with the lack of contact with his father."Currently, my Aunties are still abducted. Family and lawyers have received no update on how they are, nor why they are incarcerated. Concerning my father, there is complete silence. My brother and I have had no contact with him for more than six months. We do not even know the true state of his health," the post read.Kasim Khan also referred to protests being held in Pakistan over his father's imprisonment, saying people were continuing to demand justice and the right to be heard."Meanwhile, thousands of Pakistanis are peacefully taking to the streets to protest against his illegal and politically motivated imprisonment. However, the people of Pakistan have not given up. No barricade, intimidation or repression can muzzle the people’s demand for justice and their democratic right to be heard. There can be no lasting peace or stability while their democratic will is suppressed and their chosen leader remains behind bars,” Kasim Khan added.His remarks came a day after the families of the three detained sisters approached the Lahore High Court seeking permission for relatives and lawyers to meet them.According to Dawn, Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar filed two civil miscellaneous applications in pending writ petitions on behalf of Shah Raiz Khan, son of Aleema Khan, and Sakeena Niazi, daughter of Noreen Niazi.The pleas challenged the denial of meetings between the detained women and their family members and lawyers, and also raised the issue of access to medicines.The families have alleged that neither relatives nor legal counsel have been permitted to meet the three women or provide them with medicines. The applications stated that medicines had been provided to the sisters on only one occasion and that no one had subsequently been allowed to meet them, Dawn reported.The pleas have sought directions from the Lahore High Court allowing family members and lawyers to meet the detained women and provide them with medicines, according to Dawn.Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of PTI's September 27 protest call.The detentions came amid a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its planned countrywide demonstrations and march to Islamabad. The party had called for the protests to demand Imran Khan's release and mobilise support for the supremacy of the Constitution.On September 24, the Lahore High Court had declined a request to immediately suspend notifications ordering the preventive detention of the three sisters.Imran Khan has been in Adiala Jail since August 2023. His detention and the PTI's protests have remained at the centre of a wider political confrontation in Pakistan, with the party continuing to demand his release.
Article Summary: Kasim Khan claims his three aunts remain 'abducted' by Pakistani authorities. He also says he and his brother have had no contact with their father for six months. His aunts Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned September 27 protest.

Article Title: Pak army chief Munir bypasses PM Sharif, moves to deploy more military assets to Saudi Arabia
Article Text:
Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is built on on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistani pact under which Pakistan had sent about 8,000 troops to the kingdom by May (Photo: Agencies).

Pakistan defence forces chief Asim Munir agreed to quickly deploy more Pakistani troops to Saudi Arabia , despite the Pakistani Parliament voting to stay out of the Houthi conflict 11 years ago.The Mecca defence pact signed by Pakistan with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August was invoked for the first time on Monday, amid increasing Houthi attacks on the Saudi kingdom.According to Reuters, the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is based on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistani pact under which Pakistan had sent about 8,000 troops to the kingdom by May.Pakistan's information ministry said the alliance "has gone through all necessary government procedures".However, it did not clarify if the cabinet or parliament was involved, calling details of the deployment "a matter ​of operational confidentiality."Senior fellow for South Asia at the Atlantic ​Council, Michael Kugelman, told Reuters that Pakistan is currently in a different era, with a comparatively weaker parliament."There were times in the past when Pakistan's parliament would vote not to send ⁠troops, and the military would abide by that decision. But it's a different era now," Kugelman said.Pakistan's armed forces have often been accused of holding the reins of Islamabad’s politics.In 2025, Munir was elected as the field marshal, the chief of all defence forces in Pakistan. Constitutional changes have allowed him to hold the position till 2030, with lifetime rank as the field marshal.Munir is also immune to any criminal prosecution, signalling the military's increasing influence over the constitutional establishment.Munir is widely acknowledged to be more powerful domestically than any of his predecessors. The military has control over major government portfolios like defence and foreign relations.Jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan ’s party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), currently protesting for his release, has accused the army of dominating politics.The relationship between Imran Khan and Asim Munir has reportedly been bitter since 2019, when Munir, then director-general of Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), was removed after less than eight months in the post, reportedly at the insistence of the then-PM Khan.No official reason was given for Munir’s removal.Khan was himself ousted as prime minister in April 2022. Seven months later, in November 2022, Munir returned to the centre of Pakistan’s power structure when PM Shehbaz Sharif appointed him army chief, succeeding Bajwa.
Article Summary: Pakistan's armed forces have often been accused of holding the reins of Islamabad’s politics. Mecca defence pact signed by Pakistan with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August was invoked for the first time on Monday. Pakistan's information ministry said the alliance "has gone through all necessary government procedures"

Article Title: Pakistan bets on electric vehicles as Middle East war sends petrol prices soaring 54%
Article Text:
Pakistan fuel prices to be revised every day

Poll Vote & Share your view How do rising oil prices influence your view on transitioning to electric vehicles? Strongly encourage me to switch Have no impact on my decision 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

EV sales accelerate amid fuel price pressure

Pakistan expects to achieve its electric-vehicle adoption target ahead of schedule as surging oil prices make the shift away from petrol-powered vehicles increasingly attractive, a senior government official said.The government aims for electric vehicles to account for 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030 under its EV policy announced last year. Haroon Akhtar, adviser to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on industries and production, said the sharp rise in fuel prices has reduced the time needed for buyers to recover the higher upfront cost of EVs.“I feel that the target we had set in our electric-vehicle policy last year, we will achieve it much earlier as rise in oil prices has brought cost recovery of EV to one to one and a half year,” Akhtar told Bloomberg in Islamabad.“People are realizing the benefit now. You don't have to pay for petrol,” he said.Petrol and diesel prices in Pakistan have risen 54% and 43%, respectively, since the Middle East conflict began in February, according to data available from Pakistan State Oil Company Ltd.Akhtar said sales of electric motorcycles and scooters have tripled from a year earlier, while electric-car sales have doubled, although industry-wide EV sales data is not publicly available.“This is an impact of the Middle East conflict, as fuel prices have gone up,” Akhtar said.Despite the growing incentive to switch to EVs, factors including high vehicle costs and limited charging infrastructure mean a large-scale transformation of Pakistan’s vehicle fleet and oil consumption will take years.The government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks. It is considering tax incentives for EVs to narrow the price gap between electric and conventional vehicles, Akhtar said.
Article Summary: Pakistan aims for electric vehicles to account for 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030. The sharp rise in fuel prices has reduced the time needed for buyers to recover the higher upfront cost of EVs. The government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks.

Article Title: Pakistan forces accused of quadcopter blast that killed 2 children in Balochistan
Article Text:
Pakistan forces accused of quadcopter link

A blast in Balochistan's Panjgur district killed two children and left three others injured, The Balochistan Post reported. The incident took place in Fateh Ali Bazaar in Gowargo tehsil, where the children had been playing.According to the report, the children noticed an unidentified object hanging from a tree. The object exploded after it was disturbed, killing two boys aged nine and 10. Three other boys, aged seven, nine and 12, were injured.The nature of the device that caused the explosion remains unclear.However, local sources alleged that it was connected to a quadcopter operated by Pakistani security forces. One source also claimed that explosives had been attached to a military quadcopter and placed in the area.The source further alleged that local journalists were later told to describe the incident as a hand-grenade blast or an explosion involving another device.The Panjgur incident comes amid other allegations of civilian casualties involving military drones and quadcopters in Balochistan.On September 24, four young men were killed and two others injured in an alleged military drone strike in Balicha, Kech, according to The Balochistan Post.Families of those killed said the men had gone there for a picnic and denied claims that they were militants.The incident triggered a boycott of courts across Makran, while lawyers called for an independent probe into the deaths.Earlier on September 18, five civilians were reportedly injured in alleged quadcopter attacks in Balochabad and Bullo in the Mand area, the report said.
Article Summary: Blast in Balochistan's Panjgur district killed two children and left three others injured. Local sources alleged that it was connected to a quadcopter operated by Pakistani security forces. Incident comes amid other allegations of civilian casualties involving military drones and quadcopters.

Article Title: Nearly 3 in 4 Pakistan inmates await trial amid prison overcrowding in country: Report
Article Text:
73% of Pakistan prisoners are under-trial, HRCP report finds

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the main cause of prison overcrowding in Pakistan? Delays in the justice system Arbitrary arrests Weak bail procedures Other reasons 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan's prisons are facing severe overcrowding, with people awaiting trial making up nearly three-fourths of the country's prison population, a Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) report has found.The report, 'Beyond the Prison Wall: Reducing Overcrowding in Pakistan's Prisons', said 73.41% of inmates were under-trial in 2024. The share has gone up from 66% in 2017, The Express Tribune reported.The report said Pakistan's prisons were operating at 152.2% of their approved capacity on average during July and August 2024.The HRCP said simply building more prisons would not address the problem. It pointed to delays in the justice system, including lengthy trials, weak bail procedures and the widespread use of pre-trial detention.Punjab faces an even bigger problem. According to official figures cited by the HRCP, 74,773 prisoners were held in 45 prisons across the province in September 2026. The sanctioned capacity was 39,204, meaning the prisons were operating at nearly 191% of capacity.Of the total inmates, 54,932 were awaiting trial.Punjab has added new prisons, barracks and other facilities over the years, but the report said the additional capacity has not matched the rise in the number of prisoners.The scale of the problem has grown majorly. Punjab province had 52,803 prisoners against a capacity of 21,527 in 2010. Overcrowding in the province stood at 173.6% in 2024, according to figures cited by The Express Tribune.The HRCP blamed arbitrary arrests, delays in investigations and lengthy prosecution for the growing number of people held without conviction.As a result, many accused people remain behind bars for months or even years while waiting for investigations and court proceedings to move forward, the report said.
Article Summary: 73.41% of inmates in Pakistan's prisons were under-trial in 2024. The share has gone up from 66% in 2017, according to a Human Rights Commission of Pakistan report. The HRCP said simply building more prisons would not address the problem. Delays in the justice system, arbitrary arrests and weak bail procedures were blamed.

Article Title: 'Come to your senses': What is Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif's condition for talks with Imran's party
Article Text:
Shehbaz’s talks offer fails to sway PTI as long march presses on

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think dialogue is the best way to resolve political disagreements? Yes, dialogue can help No, other steps are needed It depends on the situation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Imran Khan-led Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Tuesday questioned the seriousness of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s offer for talks, calling it "merely symbolic" and saying the government had taken no concrete step beyond extending the invitation, Pakistan Today reported.PTI spokesperson Gohar said the Shehbaz Sharif-led government had also prevented PTI leaders from meeting the party’s founder and former PM Imran Khan , for nearly a year.Speaking to reporters in Rawalpindi, he said the last such meeting took place in October last year, Geo News reported.His remarks came after Sharif asked PTI to halt its ongoing long march towards Islamabad as a condition for holding talks.At an event in Islamabad, the prime minister warned that protests and long marches could hurt Pakistan’s economy. "I urge you to come to your senses, end the long march and sit-in, and then we will sit with you," he said.The PTI-led march, meanwhile, continued towards Peshawar on Monday, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi calling on party supporters to join the mobilisation.Afridi addressed march participants after the convoy reached Kohat and thanked residents for their "magnificent welcome". He said the convoy would resume its journey towards Peshawar from University Chowk on Tuesday, The Express Tribune reported.Declaring his loyalty to Imran Khan, Afridi said, “I am a soldier of Imran Khan. Even if the whole world comes together, it cannot put a price on me." He also urged supporters to send a message that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa belongs to Imran Khan.The chief minister had started the march from Lakki Marwat on Sunday after negotiations between PTI and the federal government failed to settle differences over the planned protest.Those talks, led by national assembly speaker Ayaz Sadiq, ended on Saturday without an agreement.The Pakistan government had asked PTI to call off the march, while the opposition sought assurances that its leaders would be permitted to meet long-imprisoned Imran Khan.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif asked PTI to halt its long march towards Islamabad as a condition for holding talks. PTI spokesperson said government had taken no concrete step beyond extending invitation. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi called on supporters to join mobilisation.

Article Title: Pakistan successfully test-fires extended version of Fatah-4 cruise missile
Article Text:
Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch.

Pakistan successfully test-fired its homemade extended version of the ground-based Fatah-4 cruise missile on Tuesday.The cruise missile is capable of engaging long-range targets with high precision, the army said. PTI reported.In a statement, Pakistan Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the “weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.”According to the Pakistan army, the test validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability.Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch.President Asif Ali Zardari , Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif , Field Marshal Asim Munir, who serves as Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, and the services chiefs praised the successful test.Pakistan had previously carried out a successful test of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile in May.The base version of Fatah-4 reportedly has a range of up to 750 kilometres and can reportedly hit targets with a five-metre accuracy.The military confirmed the new variant has an extended range but did not clarify how far.Fatah-4 is a conventional cruise missile of Islamabad’s army rocket force command. It flies at an altitude of about 50 meters to evade air defences and avoid radar detection.
Article Summary: Pakistan successfully test-fired its homemade extended version of the ground- based Fatah-4 cruise missile on Tuesday. Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch. President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Asim Munir and the services chiefs praised the successful test.

Article Title: Another showdown brewing in Pakistan? Imran Khan supporters hit streets after talks fail
Article Text:
Supporters of imprisoned Imran Khan march towards Islamabad demanding his release.

Talks between PTI, government fail

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the government response to the PTI protests? It's appropriate and necessary. It's excessive and unjustified. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Thousands of supporters of jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan began a march towards Islamabad on Sunday, demanding his release after talks between his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party and the government failed to break the political deadlock.Khan, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's main political rival, has been in prison since 2023 on corruption and other charges. Khan and his party have described the cases as politically motivated, the Associated Press reported.Despite his imprisonment, he continues to command a large and committed support base.The protesters set off from Lakki Marwat district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where PTI is in power, in a convoy of trucks, buses and cars. Organisers have planned overnight stops as the caravan makes its way towards Islamabad.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi, a staunch Khan supporter, is leading the march. Speaking from a specially designed container truck bearing a large portrait of Khan, Afridi expressed confidence that the movement would succeed in taking its demands to the heart of the capital.Authorities have erected roadblocks using shipping containers at entry points to Islamabad and at several locations inside the city.PTI and the federal government had held talks over postponing the march, but failed to reach an agreement. PTI chairman Gohar Khan said negotiations remained deadlocked after two rounds.Interior minister Mohsin Naqvi blamed Afridi for the failure of the talks and warned that he would be held responsible for any loss of life during the planned march.The government had urged PTI to postpone the protest, citing a rise in militant attacks by the Pakistani Taliban, also known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), in the northwest. The government has also accused PTI of sympathising with the TTP.PTI organisers, however, have vowed to reach Islamabad after mobilising hundreds of thousands of Khan supporters. Apart from Khan's release, protesters are demanding that he be shifted to a hospital and that his family be allowed to visit him.Officials have said Khan is in good health and receives regular family visits, but maintain that meetings with the imprisoned former prime minister cannot be used for political purposes.The march was originally scheduled for September 27 but was postponed after PTI leaders said authorities had blocked key routes to Islamabad, including the Attock Bridge, a major crossing used by convoys from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.Previous protests by Khan's supporters have turned violent. During one such protest in 2024, security personnel and civilians were killed.
Article Summary: Talks between PTI, government fail to break political deadlock. Protesters set off from Lakki Marwat district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where PTI is in power, in a convoy of trucks, buses and cars. Khan has been in prison since 2023 on corruption and other charges.

Article Title: Pakistan braces for showdown as talks collapse, Imran Khan’s party pushes ahead with march
Article Text:
Imran Khan has been incarcerated since 2023.

PTI demands access to Imran Khan

Government and PTI blame each other

Long march to begin from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the federal government negotiate further with PTI? Yes, dialogue is essential No, they should stand firm Only under certain conditions 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party will proceed with its planned long march towards Islamabad after a second round of talks with the government ended without a deal on access to jailed former prime minister Imran Khan The negotiations began at 4 pm on Saturday and continued into the early hours of Sunday, but the two sides failed to resolve their differences. The main dispute centred on PTI’s demand for an immediate meeting with Khan, including access to his personal doctor.PTI had initially planned to start the long march on September 27 but postponed it to October 4 after the federal government introduced measures aimed at preventing the protest.The party wants an immediate meeting with Khan and has demanded that he be taken to a hospital where his personal doctors can examine him.Khan, 73, has been in jail since 2023 after being convicted in a corruption case. He is currently held at the high-security Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi.PTI has also called for the release of Khan’s sisters and other people arrested ahead of the protest. It wants a proper medical examination of Khan’s wife, Bushra Bibi, and has demanded that their legal cases be heard without interference.The government, however, insisted that PTI first cancel the protest before it would consider allowing its leaders to meet Khan, according to sources. PTI rejected that condition and wanted access to its jailed leader before deciding whether to call off the march.Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayin-e-Pakistan leader Senator Allama Nasir Abbas said the negotiations had failed because the two sides could not agree on the roles of the federal and provincial governments in dealing with terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, as well as access to Khan.“No understanding could be reached regarding the respective roles of the province and the federal government concerning terrorism in the province, and the matter of a meeting with Imran Khan remains unresolved,” Abbas, who is also Leader of the Opposition in the Senate, said.“We endeavoured to reach a conclusion, but the deadlock persists -- specifically regarding access to Khan Sahib's personal physician,” he added.Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry said the talks failed mainly because the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government could not guarantee that it would cooperate with the federal government in the fight against terrorism in the future.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is governed by PTI, and the province is also where the planned march will begin.Pakistan Peoples Party leader Sherry Rehman, who took part in the negotiations, said the government delegation had discussed all the opposition's demands.“Unfortunately, the draft [agreement] was changed four times after it was agreed upon,” she told Geo News, adding that she would not go into the details.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi announced at 12:46 am that the protest would go ahead.He said supporters from Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu and Lakki Marwat would join the march at Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat at 1 pm on Sunday.The convoy is scheduled to stop near Karak for the night before leaving at 12:30 pm the following day and staying overnight near Kohat.On October 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram and Orakzai will join the convoy as it moves towards Peshawar, with the group expected to spend the night near Mattani.Afridi said the caravan would leave Budh Bair in Peshawar on the afternoon of October 7. Supporters from other parts of Peshawar will join at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza before the convoy moves towards Charsadda.“The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange,” he said.The protesters are scheduled to leave Charsadda Interchange at 12:30 pm on October 8 after supporters from Charsadda and Mohmand join them.Afridi said people from across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa would gather at Khairabad later that day before the next stage of the march is announced.“God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there,” he said.The federal government has warned that the protesters will not be allowed to enter Islamabad. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s political adviser Rana Sanaullah said authorities would prevent the march from reaching the capital.“No one would be allowed to enter Islamabad,” he told reporters.The government had earlier said it would block roads leading into Islamabad with shipping containers and deploy additional security personnel to prevent the protesters from entering the capital.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party will proceed with its planned long march towards Islamabad. The party wants an immediate meeting with Khan and has demanded that he be taken to a hospital where his personal doctors can examine him. The government, however, insisted that PTI first cancel the protest before it would consider allowing its leaders to meet Khan.

Article Title: India slams Pakistan at UN, says ‘so-called’ civilian governments serve at army’s mercy
Article Text:
Pakistan's Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif

India on Friday hit back at Pakistan at the UN General Assembly, rejecting Islamabad’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and accusing its “so-called” civilian governments of serving “at the mercy” of the army.Exercising its Right of Reply during a Third Committee meeting, first secretary at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Bhavika Mangalanandan said Pakistan’s civilian governments “rarely complete their terms”, while accusing Islamabad of using cross-border terrorism to divert attention from domestic discontent.Accoridng to news agency PTI, India “categorically” rejected Pakistan’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh were, are and will always remain “integral and inalienable” parts of India.“We all know that the so-called civilian governments in Pakistan serve at the mercy of their army and rarely complete their terms,” Mangalanandan said.Referring to jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan, she said a “former Prime Minister continues to remain in jail, even as his health is reported to be fast deteriorating.”She also said the erstwhile ruling party had not been allowed to contest elections.“Instead of addressing domestic discontent, Pakistan seeks to distract by fomenting instability in India and sponsoring, inciting, abetting, and financing cross-border terrorism in my country for more than three decades,” she said.Turning to Jammu and Kashmir, Mangalanandan said, “The only outstanding matter is a vacation of the territory Pakistan holds under illegal and forcible occupation.She accused Pakistan of attempting to divert attention from unrest in the country.“This is a desperate attempt by Pakistan to mask the ongoing tragedy in Rawalakot and its other cities, the killing of hundreds of civilians, and the brutal crackdown across Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, for merely demanding bread, electricity and human dignity,” she said.India also invoked the term “Form 47”, used in reference to allegations of rigging and manipulation in Pakistan’s 2024 general elections.“When any free media is banned from covering such news in Pakistan, the evidence becomes undeniable for the global community that only the writ of the Form 47 government and their masters and the army headquarters runs large,” she said.Contrasting this with Jammu and Kashmir, India said Assembly Elections were held there in 2024, followed by a peaceful transfer of power to an elected government.“The contrast could not have been starker. The only human rights violation taking place in Kashmir is perpetrated by the armed forces of Pakistan and their terrorist proxies. Propaganda does not become fact through repetition,” Mangalanandan said.“Pakistan would serve its people better by confronting its own fault lines and building its economy than by coveting the territory of others,” she added.
Article Summary: India “categorically” rejected Pakistan’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh were, are and will always remain “integral and inalienable”

Article Title: Pakistan kills 5 TTP militants as violence escalates on Afghanistan border
Article Text:
The militants reportedly belonged to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, which the government calls Fitna al-Khawarij (Representative image: Reuters).

Pakistani security forces killed five militants during an intelligence-based operation on Saturday in the country's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.The militants reportedly belonged to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan , which the government calls Fitna al-Khawarij.The operation was carried out in KPK's South Waziristan district, based on intelligence about several militant hideouts, PTI reported, citing an official.A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered, the official said.Pak army has been targeting such hideouts amid increased violence at the Afghanistan border.On Friday, seven militants belonging to the same group were killed in North Waziristan district. Such operations form part of Pakistan's Azm-e-Istehkam initiative, aimed at countering terrorism.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has long struggled with instability, fueled by militant violence, the movement of fighters across the border from Afghanistan, and repeated military campaigns.After its ceasefire agreement with the Pakistani government collapsed in November 2022, the TTP has launched a series of attacks in the province, which borders Afghanistan.Last week, a suicide bombing at a roadside police checkpoint in KPK's Dera Ismail Khan district killed more than a dozen security personnel and wounded at least 30 others. Nearly 21 people died in the city of Kohat after a car loaded with explosives rammed into the entrance of a mosque; both attacks were linked to the TTP.According to the Centre for Research and Security Studies, an Islamabad-based think tank, KPK was Pakistan's worst-hit region for violence in the third quarter of 2025. The region recorded around 638 violence-related deaths, nearly 71 per cent of the national total. KPK also faced 221 violent incidents, more than 67 per cent of the total.Overall, Pakistan recorded 1,232 rebel group attacks during the first nine months of 2026, according to a report by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, with the number of attacks in September reaching a 12-year high.
Article Summary: Militants reportedly belonged to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, which the government calls Fitna al-Khawarij. Operation carried out in KPK's South Waziristan district, based on intelligence about several militant hideouts. A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered.

Article Title: Pakistan logs over 1.2k rebel attacks in 9 months of ’26, security crisis deepens
Article Text: During the first nine months of 2026, Pakistan recorded 1,232 rebel group attacks, according to a report by Islamabad-based think tank Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, indicating that a major security crisis is brewing. The number of attacks in Sept reached a 12-year high, with 225 attacks resulting in 545 deaths. Police and military personnel have been the primary targets of these operations, accounting for majority of fatalities.Spearheaded by groups such as Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Baloch Liberation Army, Baloch Liberation Front and alliances like Ittehad Mujahideen Pakistan, these attacks remain concentrated in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and former tribal areas. Formed in 2025, IMP is the latest threat and comprises three sub-outfits — Hafiz Gul Bahadur group (HGBG), Lashkar-e-Islam and Harakat Inqilab-e-Islami Pakistan.Just last week, over a dozen security personnel were killed and at least 30 wounded in a suicide bombing at a roadside police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. A week before that around 21 Pakistani security personnel were killed and dozens injured in a powerful suicide bombing and subsequent firing at the police line and intelligence facility in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.The surge in Sept represents a 13% increase from 199 incidents reported in Aug, marking the third consecutive month of compounding violence.Balochistan served as the primary epicentre of the escalation, bearing the brunt of the violence with 131 recorded attacks, accounting for more than half of all nationwide incidents. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa followed with 58 attacks, while the former tribal areas recorded 34 incidents, the institute claimed. Tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have risen as Pakistan repeatedly accuses the ruling Afghan Taliban of providing safe havens and operational freedom to the TTP.
Article Summary: During the first nine months of 2026, Pakistan recorded 1,232 rebel group attacks. The number of attacks in Sept reached a 12-year high, with 225 attacks resulting in 545 deaths. Police and military personnel have been the primary targets of these operations.

Article Title: Shehbaz govt, Imran Khan’s PTI hold talks as Pakistan braces for protests
Article Text: Pakistan’s federal government and jailed former prime minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) agreed to hold a second round of talks on Saturday, as the opposition party prepares for a long march towards Islamabad from October 4.The first round of negotiations was held on Friday in the chamber of national assembly speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, who is facilitating the dialogue amid heightened security in the capital.According to a statement issued by the National Assembly Secretariat, the participants held detailed discussions “on the prevailing political situation and exchanged views on various matters of national importance”.“The government, PPP and opposition representatives apprised each other of their respective positions and held a detailed exchange of views constructively and cordially. The participants emphasised the need to resolve national issues through dialogue and negotiations,” it said, according to news agency PTI.The second round will be held at 2 pm on Saturday in the speaker’s chamber.Sadiq said he was “only playing the role of a mediator”, adding that his office was “always open” to resolving issues through negotiations.“Parliament is the only forum where solutions to issues can be found,” he said, stressing that negotiations were the way to address political differences.PTI international spokesman Zulfiqar Bukhari said the talks were “primarily aimed at defusing the current political situation surrounding PTI’s planned march/protest toward Islamabad on October 4”.Bukhari said the party’s demands included an “immediate” meeting with Khan and a decision to take him to hospital so his personal doctors could examine him. PTI has also sought the release of Khan’s sisters and others arrested ahead of the protest, a medical check-up for his wife Bushra Bibi and proper hearings in their cases.Meanwhile, the Pakistan authorities have deployed additional police and placed shipping containers on routes into Islamabad. The blockades have already disrupted freight movement.Bukhari said the long march would begin from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat, with stops planned in Karak and Kohat on October 5 before entering Peshawar district.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf to hold second round of talks on Saturday. Opposition party preparing for long march towards Islamabad from October 4. First round of negotiations was held on Friday in the chamber of national assembly speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq.

Article Title: Bangladesh party backs CJP stir, ex-Yunus aide seeks Modi's fall
Article Text: DHAKA: Hardline Jamaat-e-Islami ally and NCP convener Nahid Islam, a key member of the July 2024 movement that led to Sheikh Hasina's ouster as Bangladesh PM, backed the CJP-spearheaded protests in New Delhi, while a former adviser to the erstwhile Muhammad Yunus-led interim govt said he was waiting to witness PM Narendra Modi's downfall."The struggles of young people in Bangladesh and India are interconnected," said the convener of National Citizen Party. Young Indians are demanding electoral accountability and the protection of democratic rights, he said and asked them to "stand firm, protect one another, reject communal hatred, and refuse to surrender the future of South Asia to fascism and division"."To the democratic people of India: from Dhaka, and from the unfinished democratic aspirations of our July generation, we stand with you," Islam, who is also opposition chief whip in the Bangladesh parliament, said in a statement on X Saturday. "Hindutva majoritarianism, fascism and religious supremacy should not shape South Asia's future."He was joined by Asif Nazrul, who said, "The people of this country have suffered in various ways, falling victim to Modi and his politics; they and their families will find some solace.""Like many others, I, too, am waiting to witness Modi's downfall," said the former adviser to the interim govt under which Bangladesh-India bilateral ties nosedived.If Modi govt fell, things would change - anti-Muslim politics would suffer a setback, Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu would lose an ally and inequalities in society might be diminished, he said, adding Modi was facing pressure from "cockroach bites".Islam stressed the stud-ent-led movement against recruitment quotas had developed into an uprising against 15 years of "authoritarian rule" in Bangladesh. He brought up India's history of "democratic resistance", citing the Shaheen Bagh protests and student activism at JNU and Jadavpur University."This struggle is not yours alone. From Dhaka, we stand with you as friends bound by a common demand for accountable power, democratic institutions, and human dignity," he said.
Article Summary: Hardline Jamaat-e-Islami ally and NCP convener Nahid Islam backed the CJP- spearheaded protests in New Delhi. Former adviser to the erstwhile Muhammad Yunus-led interim govt said he was waiting to witness PM Narendra Modi's downfall.

Article Title: ‘Our seas, our land’: Sri Lanka assures India against hostile acts from its territory
Article Text:
File photo: Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake

Sri Lanka rejects requests from US, Iran

India, Sri Lanka reaffirm security cooperation

Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has assured that his country will not allow its territory or airspace to be used for activities that threaten India's security, reiterating Colombo's commitment to a strict non-aligned foreign policy amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.Addressing a public gathering at Nikaweratiya in Sri Lanka's Northwestern Province on Sunday, Dissanayake said the country would not permit hostile actions against its neighbour.“Our seas, our land would never be allowed to be used for any hostile act against our neighbour India,” he said, according to news agency PTI.Recalling his government's foreign policy record over the past two years, Dissanayake said Sri Lanka would continue to follow a non-aligned approach and would not take sides in military conflicts.“We are not a nation of any military capabilities, so we would not become party to any military conflict,” he said.Dissanayake said Sri Lanka had rejected requests from both the United States and Iran amid the ongoing conflict between the two sides.He said Colombo had denied permission for US aircraft to land in Sri Lanka and also turned down Iran's request to send warships.“But we won’t hesitate when asked for humanitarian assistance,” the Sri Lankan president said.In March, Sri Lanka provided hospital care to sailors from an Iranian vessel that was struck by a US submarine.Dissanayake's latest remarks follow a meeting with Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in Colombo last month, during which the two sides discussed their broad partnership, including cooperation on regional safety, security, peace and prosperity.During the meeting, Dissanayake reiterated that Sri Lanka would not allow its territory to be used for activities inimical to India's security interests.Singh, who was on a three-day visit to Sri Lanka, also conveyed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's greetings to Dissanayake and congratulated him on completing two years in office.The two countries reaffirmed their commitment to working together as close neighbours and maritime partners for the development and welfare of their people, while supporting regional security.Dissanayake's latest statement reiterates Colombo's position that its territory and airspace will not be used for hostile activities against India, while maintaining its stated policy of staying out of military conflicts.
Article Summary: Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake reiterates country's commitment to non-aligned foreign policy. He says Sri Lanka will not allow its territory or airspace to be used for activities that threaten India's security. President says country rejected requests from US and Iran amid ongoing conflict.
